## Overview

**This is a comparator, not the model of record.** It is [LRPLF07](../lrp-rli-lf-007/index.qmd) restricted to the two waves at which randomisation alone separates the arms — the pre-randomisation baseline t1 and the end of the randomised period t2 (#584 decision 3). Same model, same adjustment set, same estimand.

The four-wave model shares its baseline arm gap, child effects, dispersion and group-by-ability term across waves. Later observations can therefore affect the t2 estimate. This two-wave fit measures sensitivity to that use of later data. It uses the same randomised comparison and is not an independent replication.

Read the four-wave report for the levels view across all four timepoints — showing them on one scale is that model's purpose, and this restriction gives it up.

LRPLF207 is a **level-factors** model for CELF basic concepts (`celf`): what is associated with the score *level* at the two fitted timepoints, t1 and t2 (Beta-Binomial logit, child random intercept; no own baseline).

_Causal labelling + level-model crossover caveat._ Every non-randomised coefficient is an **adjusted association** under the DAG. The group effect is `group x time`, parameterised as the covariate-adjusted arm gap at t1 (`arm_gap_t1`, a pre-randomisation *balance* quantity, never an effect) plus the change in that gap at each later wave (`d_grp_time[t]`; #552): after t2 the waitlist crosses over, so the **clean randomised contrast lives only at t2** — the t2 change `d_grp_time[t2]`, a difference-in-differences of adjusted levels, labelled *causal*; the only later wave in this fit is t2, so the model carries `arm_gap_t1` and `d_grp_time[t2]` alone — the post-crossover waves are not fitted here at all, which is the point of the comparator. SES excluded (non-DAG / redundant).

## Model

Beta-Binomial$(N, \mu\kappa, (1-\mu)\kappa)$ on the level count, $N = 18$, with
$\operatorname{logit}\mu_{t} = \alpha + \alpha_{\text{time}[t]} + b_{\text{grp}[t]}\text{group} + \gamma_A A_{\text{std},t} + g_{\text{ability}[t]}z(\text{blocks}) + \gamma_{\text{grp\_ability}}\,\text{group}\,z(\text{blocks}) + u_{\text{child}}$.
